l: The City (Al-Balad), The City (Al-Balad), Surah 90: The City (Al-Balad)
s: The City (Al-Balad) is presented as the place by which the speaker swears, where the addressee dwells. Man is created in an atmosphere, given eyes, a tongue, two lips, and guidance to the mountain ways, yet some think no one has power over or sees them and boast of destroying wealth. The Ascent is identified with freeing a slave, feeding someone in the day of hunger, helping an orphan near of kin or a poor wretch in misery, and believing while exhorting one another to perseverance and pity. Believers are assigned the right hand, while disbelievers who reject the revelations are assigned the left hand, with Fire as an awning over them.

l: Surah 92: The Night (Al-Lail), Surah 92: The Night (Al-Lail), Surah 92: The Night (Al-Lail)
s: Surah 92: The Night (Al-Lail) contrasts the night and day and declares that human effort is directed toward different ends. It describes the generous and dutiful person who believes in goodness as being eased toward ease, while the hoarding and self-sufficient person who disbelieves in goodness is eased toward adversity. It warns that the flaming Fire is endured by the most wretched person, who denies and turns away, while the righteous are kept far from it. The righteous give their wealth seeking the purpose of their Lord Most High and will be content.
